title: Reductive group schemes have universal invariant power lifting
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $G\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ a smooth affine finitely presented group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with the group-object diagrams interpreted over $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Finite presentation means locally finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Suppose every geometric fibre is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] and has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup; over its algebraically closed residue field, unipotent means that all matrices in a faithful finite-dimensional representation are unipotent. For every commutative $R$-algebra $R'$, put $G'=G\times_R R'$ [def-pc-base-change] and $C'=\Gamma(G',\mathcal O_{G'})$. For every equivariant surjective homomorphism $u:E\twoheadrightarrow F$ of commutative $R'$-algebras with $G'$-actions, and every $b\in F^{G'}$, there exist $N\geq1$ and $a\in E^{G'}$ with $u(a)=b^N$. An action here is an algebra coaction $\rho_E:E\to E\otimes_{R'}C'$ (and similarly for $F$) satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities from multiplication and identity in $G'$, and $E^{G'}=\{e\in E:\rho_E(e)=e\otimes1\}$; equivariance means $(u\otimes1)\rho_E=\rho_Fu$. The algebras $E,F$ are arbitrary, without finite-generation or flatness assumptions.

source.place: Alper, Adequate moduli spaces and geometrically reductive group schemes, Theorem 9.7.5, Proposition 9.3.1(i), Lemma 9.2.5(2),(3), printed pp.522,524,527--528. WANTED local copy; read https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf.

proof.text: First work over a DVR $A$ with algebraically closed residue field and a split semisimple simply connected $H$. Fix a finite free rational module $V$ and primitive $v\in V^H$. Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-primitive-endomorphism-detector] to get $W,\phi$. Since $\phi(v)$ is invariant and the invariant endomorphisms are precisely scalars, write $\phi(v)=c\,\mathrm{id}_W$. Its nonzero reduction implies $c\notin\mathfrak m$: otherwise every matrix entry would reduce to zero. Thus $c$ is a unit. Indeed a nonunit generates a proper ideal contained in the unique maximal ideal of the local ring. Replace $\phi$ by $c^{-1}\phi$, obtaining $\phi(v)=\mathrm{id}_W$.

Choose a basis of $W$, of rank $d>0$. Put $f=\det\circ\phi$. The determinant formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] shows that $f$ is a degree-$d$ polynomial in the linear coordinate forms of $\phi$, hence an element of $\operatorname{Sym}^d_A(V^\vee)$. For every commutative $A$-algebra $D$ and $h\in H(D)$, equivariance gives $\phi_D(hx)=h\phi_D(x)h^{-1}$. The square-matrix specialization of [lem-weil-pbc-cauchy-binet] gives $\det(hTh^{-1})=\det(h)\det(T)\det(h^{-1})=\det(T)$, because applying the same formula to $hh^{-1}=I$ gives $\det(h)\det(h^{-1})=1$. These are polynomial identities, including on the universal point of the affine space of $V$, so they say that $f$ is invariant as a coaction, not merely invariant on $A$-points. Finally $f(v)=\det I=1$. This proves the primitive-polynomial hypothesis of the next step.

The group $H$ is smooth, hence flat by [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion]. Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-primitive-polynomial-lifting-criterion] to the primitive-polynomial property just proved. It gives $P(A,H)$: every equivariant module surjection onto the trivial module $A$ lifts $1$ in some positive symmetric degree, with arbitrary source module. We have proved this for every split semisimple simply connected group over every DVR with algebraically closed residue field. This is exactly the premise of [lem-sfb-reductive-symmetric-power-dvr-reduction]. Its conclusion gives $P(R,G)$ for the group in the item. The hypothesis on its geometric unipotent radical, the smoothness, affineness and finite presentation are precisely those in that node.

Fix a commutative $R$-algebra $R\prime$, an equivariant surjective homomorphism $u:E\twoheadrightarrow F$ of commutative $R\prime$-algebras with $G\prime=G\times_R R\prime$-actions, and $b\in F^{G\prime}$. Put $C=\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $C\prime=R\prime\otimes_R C$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] identifies $E\otimes_{R\prime}(R\prime\otimes_R C)$ with $E\otimes_R C$: the map sends $e\otimes(r\prime\otimes c)$ to $r\prime e\otimes c$, with inverse $e\otimes c\mapsto e\otimes(1\otimes c)$. The same formulas work for $F$. They transfer the coaction identities and equivariance directly on pure tensors, and identify the two definitions of invariance. Regard $E,F$ as rational $G$-modules over $R$. The ring $C$ is flat over $R$ by [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion, lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. Define the $R$-module $M=\{(e,r)\in E\oplus R:u(e)=rb\}$. It is the kernel of the equivariant linear map $(e,r)\mapsto u(e)-rb$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], tensoring this kernel sequence with $C$ is exact, so the diagonal coaction on $E\oplus R$ restricts to $M$; coassociativity follows by the same injectivity after tensoring twice, and counit by the inclusion. Projection $\lambda:M\to R$ is equivariant and surjective: choose $e_0$ with $u(e_0)=b$, and $(re_0,r)$ lifts $r$.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5(5) implies (3), via Lemma 4.1.8, printed pp.503--504,522; restriction of scalars makes arbitrary R-prime explicit; https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf

proof.text: Apply $P(R,G)$ from step 3 to $\lambda$ to obtain $N\geq1$ and invariant $q\in\operatorname{Sym}^N_R M$ with $\operatorname{Sym}^N(\lambda)(q)=1$. The map $t:M\to E$, $(e,r)\mapsto e$, induces an algebra homomorphism $\widetilde t:\operatorname{Sym}_R M\to E$ by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. It is equivariant: the two algebra maps to $E\otimes_R C$ agree on every generator by equivariance of $t$, so the uniqueness clause proves equality. Consequently $a=\widetilde t(q)$ is invariant. On a degree-$N$ product $(e_1,r_1)\cdots(e_N,r_N)$, $u\widetilde t$ takes value $\prod_i u(e_i)=\prod_i(r_i b)=(\prod_i r_i)b^N$. Such products span degree $N$ by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded], so linearity gives $u(a)=b^N\operatorname{Sym}^N(\lambda)(q)=b^N$. Step 4 identifies this invariance with $G\prime$-invariance, completing every base-change case. Neither $E,F$ nor $M$ needed to be finite or flat.
